native_test_cmd: python3 -m pytest tests/test_bucket_all.py tests/test_fixed_window.py -m inmemory -q --tb=line && python3 -m pytest tests/test_coverage_extras.py::test_rate_item_str tests/test_coverage_extras.py::test_inmemory_put_weight_zero_returns_true -q --tb=line
workload: Construct and retain 100000 RateItems, one per unit of an in-memory sliding window of 100000 requests.
notes: Each RateItem stores name, timestamp, and weight on a per-instance __dict__ (the class has no __slots__). tracemalloc counts 200002 live blocks for 100000 items: two blocks per item (the instance and that dict) plus the result list. A slots class with the same three fields measured 1 block per item on this interpreter, so the same workload would drop 100000 allocations (and about 3.2 MiB) while str(), attribute access, and the stored values stay the same. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 5 runs. Overlap: rate.py is not in open PRs #324, #326, #327, #329, nor in PRs merged since 2026-10-12 (#306, #317, #318, #320, #321, #322, #325, #328, #330). Not dexhunter's GCRA.step (#328). Open issue #323 is iterable limiting on the limiter, not RateItem.

native_test_cmd: python3 -m pytest tests/test_bucket_all.py tests/test_fixed_window.py -m inmemory -q --tb=line && python3 -m pytest tests/test_coverage_extras.py::test_rate_item_str tests/test_coverage_extras.py::test_inmemory_put_weight_zero_returns_true -q --tb=line
workload: One InMemoryBucket.put of weight 300000 into an empty bucket limited to 300000 per day, a bulk job charging the whole daily quota at once.
notes: The weight>1 branch does self.items.extend([item for _ in range(item.weight)]), which builds a second list of `weight` references beside the log the sliding window has to keep. Peak during that put is 5001672 bytes. Extending from itertools.repeat(item, weight) instead peaks at about 2400048 bytes for the same 300000 references (about 2.48 MiB lower) and still stores that one RateItem repeated weight times, so peek/count stay the same. test_bucket_all puts weight 10 and 20 through this branch. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 5 runs. Overlap: in_memory_bucket.py is not in open PRs #324, #326, #327, #329, nor in PRs merged since 2026-10-12 (#306, #317, #318, #320, #321, #322, #325, #328, #330). Not dexhunter's GCRA.step (#328).

native_test_cmd: python3 -m pytest tests/test_sqlite_bucket.py tests/test_bucket_all.py tests/test_fixed_window.py -m sqlite -q --tb=line
workload: SQLiteBucket.leak on an in-memory database of 120000 timestamped rows, expiring the oldest 100000.
notes: leak() runs COUNT of item_timestamp < leak_bound, then DELETE WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid ORDER BY item_timestamp ASC LIMIT count), which materializes rowids before deleting. Median 46.4519 ms over 5 warm runs, noise (max-min)/median. A single DELETE FROM rate_bucket WHERE item_timestamp < ? uses the existing timestamp index, returns the same row count, and left the same survivors on a duplicate-timestamp boundary (3 rows below the bound, the two rows on the bound kept). That statement measured about 23.9 ms on this log, roughly 22 ms less per call. Open leak PRs #329 and merged #330/#322 edit the scheduler in abstracts/bucket.py, not this query. sqlite_bucket.py is not in open PRs #324, #326, #327, #329 or PRs merged since 2026-10-12. Not GCRA.step (#328).

native_test_cmd: python3 -m pytest tests/test_sqlite_bucket.py tests/test_bucket_all.py tests/test_fixed_window.py -m sqlite -q --tb=line
workload: SQLiteBucket._peek_timestamp(999999) on a full 1000000-row daily log, the oldest-row lookup a denied weight-1 put uses for retry-after.
notes: _peek_timestamp issues SELECT * ORDER BY item_timestamp DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET offset. A full bucket denying weight 1 asks for offset limit-1, so SQLite walks nearly every index entry: median 18.3848 ms over 5 steady calls, noise (max-min)/median. The same timestamp is ORDER BY item_timestamp ASC LIMIT 1 OFFSET (count-1-offset). When the log is full and weight is 1 that forward offset is 0, an index edge read measured under 0.1 ms, so this call drops by more than 10 ms and still returns the oldest item_timestamp. COUNT(*) on this table was about 0.1 ms. Denial tests in test_fixed_window and test_bucket_all drive this lookup. sqlite_bucket.py is not in open PRs #324, #326, #327, #329 or PRs merged since 2026-10-12 (#306, #317, #318, #320, #321, #322, #325, #328, #330). Not dexhunter's GCRA.step (#328).
